fields.expected: A bit of context on how I work. Most of my experience is in building systems where the interesting part is the constraints around the model, not the model itself. At Summer Atlantic Capital I build the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system: event ingestion, temporal sequence modeling over event streams, a versioned FastAPI detection service, and a learning-to-rank layer, because an anomaly system that fires too often just creates a second problem. I also built a browser automation agent in TypeScript where every mutating capability sits behind fail-closed flags and every application moves through an explicit state machine, and where a capability is only called working once it has been validated against the level of reality it claims to support, not just a local fixture. That habit of specifying states, failure modes, and verification levels before claiming something works is what I would bring to systems engineering work. I am a U.S. citizen authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship, and I am comfortable being handed a piece of a larger system and expected to own it, document it, and test it.
